item.title: The live-action Stranger Things prequel series has its first teaser trailer and a 2028 release window, Netflix has announced.
item.description:
The live-action Stranger Things prequel series has its first teaser trailer and a 2028 release window, Netflix has announced.
“Before Hawkins, there was Marion,” reads the tagline. The show is called Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure, and it’s from The Duffer Brothers and Kate Trefry.
Before Hawkins, there was Marion.Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure. A new series only on Netflix. 2028. https://t.co/NvISItwYAF
The series is a prequel set in the 1950s, before Stranger Things and before the stage play Stranger Things: The First Shadow, which explores Henry Creel’s troubled past in Hawkins in 1959. Specifically, the teaser confirms April 19, 1955, in Marion, Nevada. We see a discarded bike outside a fenced off restricted area. "Use of deadly force authorized," reads the warning sign. The camera pans up to reveal a mystery facility lit up at night, before we move to focus on the sky above. Then there's a blink and you'll miss it look at what seems to be a UFO.
Golden Globe-winning director Joe Wright is set to direct the first three episodes of the new series, with production to take place in New Mexico. Expect a new era, setting and all-new characters, themes and mythology, Netflix added.
Jinny Howe, Netflix Head of Scripted Series, US & Canada: “Stranger Things has always belonged to the fans, and their passion made it a worldwide phenomenon. Today, on Stranger Things Day, we’re honored to partner again with Matt and Ross Duffer and Kate Trefry to give fans a new dimension of this universe to step into. Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure takes us to the 1950s with new heroes and all the heart, mystery, and spectacle of the original series. We’re proud to keep building this world with the Duffers, Kate, Shawn Levy, and Joe Wright, and we can’t wait for fans to see what’s next.”
Stranger Things Season 5 Finale Trailer Images
Co-Creators/Executive Producers Matt & Ross Duffer commented: “We’ve been dreaming of Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure for many years now, and to see it become a reality is surreal and exhilarating. We’re so grateful to our incredible team of collaborators: our showrunner Kate Trefry, who has been in the trenches with us since Season 2 and wrote Stranger Things: The First Shadow; and our director, Joe Wright, a brilliant artist whose work we’ve long admired. We can’t wait for you to see what they’re cooking up. It’s Stranger Things, but also thrillingly fresh, with a new setting, new heroes and villains, and new… actually, we’re not allowed to say any more. Now, on to casting. In the meantime -- watch the skies, nerds!”
Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure is far from the first Stranger Things spinoff we've seen from Netflix since the hit show came to an end in January, but it does promise to answer some burning questions left by the end of Season 5.
Warning! Spoilers for Stranger Things Season 5 Episode 8, The Rightside Up, follow:
In the Season 5 finale, we see Henry Creel / Vecna finally face his greatest fear: the traumatic memory of the day he was infected by the Mind Flayer and gained his powers. In this scene set inside Henry’s mind, we finally find out what was inside the briefcase that child Henry opens after bludgeoning its previous owner, an unnamed scientist, to death. Inside is a mysterious rock, which glows with an unknown energy before fusing with Henry. This, we understand, is how Henry became one with the Mind Flayer, and sets in motion all the events of Stranger Things that followed.
But what was this rock exactly, and how did it come to be in our world in the first place? An article on Netflix published as Stranger Things came to an end confirms the rock contains Mind Flayer particles, which then possess Henry. “Come find me,” the Mind Flayer beckons. And the dying scientist warns: “It will consume you.”
In a subsequent interview with Variety, Stranger Things co-creators Matt and Ross Duffer teased that the planned spinoff, which we now know to be Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure, will explain all — and answer other plot threads left dangling.
“The spinoff is going to delve into that and explain that, and you’re going to understand it,” Matt Duffer said of the briefcase rock. “But it’s a completely different mythology. So it’s not a deep exploration of the Mind Flayer or anything like that. It’s very fresh and very new, but yes, it will answer some of the loose threads that are remaining.”
Stranger Things: The First Shadow Gallery
The briefcase scene is explained in vague terms by Stranger Things: The First Shadow, the canon play that acts as a prequel to the events of the Netflix show. We've run through the plot of the play already, but in summary, it confirms that Henry and the scientist are transported to what was then known as Dimension X. When Henry returns, he is much changed, and Dr. Brenner (Matthew Modine) eventually uses him as part of his experiments in Hawkins National Laboratory.
But even before then, the play tells us of a 1943 United States experiment to turn submarines invisible during World War 2. As part of this, they travel to Dimension X. Perhaps that's where the mysterious rock originally came from, and how it ended up in our world in the first place.
The Duffers previously described the spinoff as a “clean slate.” “Completely new characters, new town, new world, new mythology,” Matt Duffer said, adding: “No common characters.”
While you wait to find out more, check out the Duffer brothers explaining the ambiguity of Eleven’s ending.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Composer Caisheng Bo talked to IGN as the official game soundtrack is released for streaming and purchase.
item.description:
Phantom Blade Zero composer Caisheng Bo is known as a pioneer in Chinese experimental music. As the soundtrack for the critically acclaimed action game gets announced for release today – a four-disc, 81-track audio adventure published by Milan Records – the music publisher shares the intriguing backstory of this soundtrack. "The musical story of Phantom Blade Zero began 18 years ago, when Caisheng Bo and Soulframe Liang—one in high school and the other in graduate school—were working on their indie game Rainblood 2: City of Flames, which would later evolve into the Phantom Blade franchise."
Bo, based in Beijing and a graduate of the University of Virginia in the US, spoke with IGN on the eve of the soundtrack's release.
IGN: From what I've seen of Phantom Blade Zero, the music very much ties in with some of the folklore and cultural themes explored in the game. Can you discuss how you sought to express this through music?
Bao: In traditional Chinese music, each instrument has developed a rigid set of associations—what it represents and how it should be used. I see this as a form of stereotyped expression. The erhu, a Chinese two-string bowed fiddle, is most often used to depict heroic action and the sorrow of personal endeavour. The pipa, a Chinese four-string lute, is associated with a feminine image and with danger on the battlefield. Anything outside these conventions may seem out of context.
This is the narrative I want to challenge in the music of Phantom Blade Zero. For each Chinese instrument, I set up a polarity between its traditional associations and a new set of meanings.
In Phantom Blade Zero, the erhu represents heroic action, as in the traditional idiom, but it also represents "manipulation"—a key image in which red threads descend from the sky, pulling enemies upward and controlling them. The pipa is tied not only to danger and the crisis lingering in the dark, but also to "discordance," an otherworldly realm where time stops and space distorts. The matouqin and Hoomai (throat singing), represent "mandate" and righteousness, while at the other pole they evoke megalophobia—the fear of vast objects. The xūn, a Chinese clay ocarina, is traditionally used to represent weeping, one of its signature playing techniques. In Phantom Blade Zero, the xun is also heard when Mu Tianmiao, a character of absolute authority, is present. These narrative polarities are among the design choices I made to enrich the game's story through music.
Alongside this innovative use of Chinese instruments, there are stuttering sound designs in the cutscenes, especially when Zuo Shang is plotting his scheme. As the story progresses, the stuttering sound grows louder and more present. This building stutter suggests his growing ambition—his uncontainable "Sha Qi" (killing intent).
By incorporating traditional Chinese instruments alongside modern musical genres and elements, I hope the music can cross cultural barriers, reach players' hearts, and offer them a truly distinct listening experience.
IGN: What other works of art inspired you for this project?
Bao: The music of the Phantom Blade series dates back almost 18 years to an indie game called Rainblood—that is where I began composing for this franchise. The music of Phantom Blade Zero is therefore built largely on what I have written over the years, though it has since developed into something uniquely its own. Most of the melodies have been carried over, but the stuttering sound design and the polarity between traditional and new meanings are entirely new.
IGN: How did your score evolve as you saw the game come together over the course of development?
Bao: Over the course of development, alongside a complete script, Soulframe would send me in-game footage of an area once they felt it was about 60% complete. They would play through the entire area—exploring hidden paths, defeating enemies, and finding treasures—just as a player would. As a result, I would regularly receive 4-hour-long video recordings for different areas of the game. I would then divide these areas into segments and plan the music for each one. In essence, I work as both music director and composer, which means I know where the music should start and what emotions it needs to capture. Once the team receives my music demo, they fine-tune the map, the combat, and the boss fights to match my music, ensuring that the game and the music sync perfectly with each other.
IGN: What are you hoping players take away from Phantom Blade Zero's soundtrack?
Bao: In vague terms, I would describe the ethnic Chinese music most listeners are familiar with as beautiful ancient villages or sacred temples—something that looks as if it has come straight out of an ink-wash painting, surrounded by tall mountains, beautiful waterfalls, and tall, sharp parasol trees. Because of Phantom Blade's unique concept of Kungfu Punk, I was able to make bold musical decisions to match the visuals. For Phantom Blade Zero, then, I want to introduce the modern side of Chinese music—think of Shanghai, a city of skyscrapers and flashy neon that is undeniably Chinese.
Beyond the question of the music's origins, I believe music is a universal language we all speak. I wanted to show the endless possibilities of combining Eastern ethnic elements with Western modern genres such as pop, trap, and metal—and how we can all appreciate the aesthetically astonishing results, regardless of cultural differences.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Elon Musk has confirmed plans to "wind down" production of the Cybertruck at Tesla's gigafactory.
item.description:
Elon Musk has confirmed plans to wind down production of the Cybertruck at Tesla's gigafactory in Texas.
“Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production,” Musk tweeted today.
Musk’s tweet left the door open to further production elsewhere, but Cybertruck lead engineer Wes Morrill then suggested that Cybertruck was being discontinued. “Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab,” he tweeted. “Thanks to everyone who contributed to making the future looking like the future. As well to the community of owners whose adventures I've enjoyed and will continue to follow.”
Tesla Cybertruck Official Release - Slideshow
The angular Cybertruck launched in 2023 to much fanfare, but sales have been poor. Indeed, the truck has suffered online ridicule ever since it was introduced in 2019, when Musk himself shattered its supposed unbreakable glass during a live demo.
Musk’s announcement was met with a mixture of mocking social media posts and mourning from Tesla devotees. “Did even last five years. Pathetic,” one person said. “It was already a bad enough day without this news. I need a second one!” another said.
In a tweet reply to one disappointed fan, Musk insisted the Cybertruck fleet “will be around for a long time.” Morrill replied to a fan who said they felt like "I lost a child" to say that Tesla would maintain spare parts and service support would continue.
Earlier this year, amid slow sales and tough questions about Cybertruck, Musk said it was "way more awesome than people realise." In April, the tech billionaire said Cybertruck was the "best product Tesla has ever made to date.”
The focus, now, is on Cybercab, which Musk has said will play a crucial role in Tesla’s robotaxi plans. According to Reuters, the two-seater robotaxi is still a small program, with production beginning only earlier this year. Tesla has listed an installed capacity of more than 125,000 units.

item.title: Rockstar may officially release GTA 6 on PC soon after console over concern about AI-generated clones, one former developer has said.
item.description:
Rockstar may officially release GTA 6 on PC soon after console over concern about AI-generated clones, one former developer has said.
In an interview with IGN sister site RPS, former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar Games may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible, due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports.
People are using AI to create clones of popular games and release them on platforms they're not normally available on. We've seen everything from Minecraft playable on X/Twitter to modders shoving Minecraft and Elden Ring together. Indeed, last month, Rockstar's own Grand Theft Auto 5 was made playable in a browser before it was pulled offline.
Seemingly in response, Anthropic issued an update for Claude that made it harder for people to use the AI model to generate video game clones, but concern that GTA 6 could pop up on PC soon after it hits PlayStation and Xbox remains.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
There is also concern around the security of the PS5, with Sony seemingly engaged in a game of Whac-a-Mole with hackers who are trying to jailbreak the latest firmware ahead of the release of GTA 6. This in turn has sparked concern that if a PS5 jailbreak is made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6 to run, then it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and maybe even made available on PC.
"[Generative AI] really has changed the world," Vermeij said, "and I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together. Obviously, I don't really know what they're thinking.
"I don't really see how you could protect against that, to be honest. I don't see it. But a big company like Take-Two, they would be able to get the lawyers on the case, and for a big game, maybe the AI doesn't really do a particularly good job.
“But yeah, I mean, it's a brave new world. What was the case before, is that there's so much effort in developing the game, that it is not possible to rip it off, and that's completely changed now. So, yeah, we're going to have to see in the next couple of years how that's going to pan out."
In October, GamesBeat reported that Rockstar was indeed planning to release GTA 6 on PC during the first quarter of 2027. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two did not comment on the report.
If true, it would mean GTA 6 hitting PC just a few months after it launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19, 2026. Some had anticipated a longer wait for the game on PC, given it took nearly two years for GTA 5 to launch on PC after consoles.
The PC launch may tie into the release of GTA 6's multiplayer mode, which fans are calling GTA Online 2 while they wait for official word from Rockstar. While Rockstar has yet to confirm an online mode for GTA 6, last month Twitch boss Dan Clancy said GTA Online 2 — or whatever GTA 6’s multiplayer mode is called — will launch next year.
Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick has always responded with vague comments when asked about the prospect of launching GTA 6 on PC, pointing to Rockstar for announcements. In May, Zelnick told Bloomberg that Rockstar "always starts on console because I think with regard to a release like that you're judged by serving the core. Like really serving the core consumer. If your core consumer isn't there, if they're not served first and best, you kind of don't hit your other consumers.”
Red Dead Redemption, GTA 5, LA Noire, Max Payne 3, and Red Dead Redemption 2 all came to PC after consoles. And while GTA's core audience may be on console, it has a huge fanbase of active players on PC, fueled by GTA Online and role-play servers.
We’ve got plenty more on GTA 6, including an unlikely gameplay reveal in the latest episode of South Park, how GTA 6 named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme, and how GTA 6's map will open up relatively early and let you explore freely.
Analysts expect GTA 6 will make over $5 billion in launch week alone. GTA 6 is scheduled to be released on November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.
If GTA 6 was confirmed for PC in early 2027, would you skip the console launch and wait to play it?

item.title: Nier: Automata got a patch yesterday to add support for more languages to the game (Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese), but it accidentally bloated the game file size to 366GB on PC. That’s 1.5 copies of GTA 6!
item.description:
Nier: Automata got a patch yesterday to add support for more languages to the game (Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese), but it accidentally bloated the game file size to 366GB on PC. That’s 1.5 copies of GTA 6!
A bug caused the entire game to be applied to every DLC pack included in the PC edition, ballooning the overall file size to Call of Duty-esque heights. Nier was previously around 50GB to download.
The game saw a wave of negative reviews come in on Steam following the patch, with players complaining that they were unable to play or, you know, download any other games.
"Claude, please add new language support for my game, no mistakes, masterpiece. It's 366 gigabytes now? Splendid,” said one review, making a joke about Square Enix using AI. “Undeniably good game which I've had to remove from my computer because some genius, presumably misusing automated tools, packed it into itself six times over, making a 360 gig install file. I'll recommend this game after it is fixed,” said another.
“I think the funniest part about the ‘slight’ issue with the new update for language support is the Steam page still lists a 50gb storage requirement. Good one guys,” reads another negative review. “Played this on PS4 loved it but 366GB is unacceptable for a company like them... fix this Square or I will STOP my FF14 sub,” read another.
Square Enix has offered a workaround for the Nier: Automata issue as it works on a fix. “We have confirmed an issue where, following the latest update to the Steam version of Nier: Automata, the installation process indicates that more storage space is required than expected,” the company said in a Japanese tweet.
“We are currently investigating the cause and working on a solution. We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. As a temporary workaround, you can download the base game by unchecking the DLC under Steam → Properties → DLC.”
Of course, Nier fans are desperate for a proper follow-up to Nier: Automata, but so far nothing has been announced. In November last year, Yoko Taro said he’d been working on various projects, but they just keep getting canceled. “I often get told stuff like, ‘Why aren’t you making a new sequel to NieR?’ or, ‘Yoko Taro isn’t doing anything,’ but that’s because recently, a lot of projects I was involved in got discontinued midway through development," he said.
"I’ve actually been working on some stuff, it’s just that it never ended up seeing the light of day. I got paid for it, so I personally have no issues with that, but people seem to think that I haven’t been doing anything just because none of the work I’ve done is being released."
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Benjamin McDaniel, who calls himself The Pilot Picasso, just unveiled his new masterpiece: a GTA 6 mural drawn by flying his plane. Using flight path visualization systems, you can watch his entire journey and see the artwork come to life.
item.description:
Benjamin McDaniel, who calls himself The Pilot Picasso, just unveiled his new masterpiece: a GTA 6 mural drawn by flying his plane. Using flight path visualization systems, you can watch his entire journey and see the artwork come to life.
It’s kind of like an Etch A Sketch because it’s a continuous line from start to finish, which is part of what makes the feat so impressive. The other thing that makes it impressive is, you know, he kept the plane in the sky the entire time.
He took off from Bentonville (QTV) airstrip at 11.29am and landed back at the same airport at 19:37pm. It took him eight hours and eight minutes to complete the piece, which he traced in the sky with a Cessna Skylane RG. The feat was completed on November 5 and you can check it out on FlightRadar24. Here’s a tweet showcasing the finished thing:
The turns to make the alligator were the most fun to watch. Well done @thepilotpicasso.https://t.co/RFlMh800Kf https://t.co/Gz3ee7QYtJ
The artwork showed the GTA 6 logo next to an alligator, palm trees, a sports car, and a bikini clad woman. A helicopter hovered above the logo.
His upcoming projects include a classical piece and a Thanksgiving piece. In a recent interview, he said, “Safety is number one. If bad weather rolls around, I push the flight to another day or another week.”
In October, The Pilot Picasso flew a route that traced out the Mona Lisa, and previously he also flew Edvard Munch’s The Scream. Previous pop culture artworks include The Lord of The Rings, Skyrim, and Spider-Man.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
We’ve got plenty more on GTA 6 while you wait for its November 19 release date, including an unlikely gameplay reveal in the latest episode of South Park, how GTA 6 named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme, and how GTA 6's map will open up relatively early and let you explore freely.
Analysts expect GTA 6 will make over $5 billion in launch week alone, so expect it to fill your feeds for a few weeks. GTA 6 is scheduled to be released on November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.

item.title: After Buying EA, Silver Lake and PIF Are Reportedly Now Seeking to Acquire Gaming Software Provider Unity
item.description:
A consortium of investors including private equity firm Silver Lake Partners and Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund PIF has held recent talks to acquire gaming software provider Unity.
A Reuters report citing confidential sources familiar with the matter states that PIF and Silver Lake, the latter of which already owns 8% of Unity, approached the company in recent weeks. The buyer consortium discussed a valuation of about $25 billion before Unity’s latest earnings report, which lifted its market capitalization to roughly $21.5 billion.
Unity has reportedly been consulting with an investment bank to evaluate its options following the approach, however talks are preliminary and no deal is assured.
Should the acquisition go ahead, this would be another major investment into the games industry for Silver Lake and PIF. The two firms previously teamed up with Jared Kushner’s Affinity Partners to acquire Electronic Arts for $55 billion in a deal that was finalised in August. Since then the publisher has initiated major corporate restructurings and studio closures, most recently shutting development studio BioWare and cancelling the next Mass Effect game.
Unity’s popular game engine and development tools have been used to create thousands of mobile, console, and PC games. These include Genshin Impact, Hollow Knight, Among Us, Subnautica, and Beat Saber, to name just a few. Notably, Unity’s tools are also used by Scopely, the developer of Monopoly Go!, and Niantic, the maker of Pokemon Go, both of which are owned by a group that includes Silver Lake, PIF, and Affinity Partners.
Silver Lake has already invested $400 million into Unity and with its 8% stake it remains one of its largest shareholders. Since going public in 2020, Unity has expanded beyond its game engine business into advertising technology and broader real-time 3D software, and its tools are increasingly used in automotive design, filmmaking, architecture, and industrial simulation.
After news of the acquisition talks first broke, Unity shares rose nearly 15% in regular trading and sit at $48.80 per share at the time of writing.
Tristan Ogilvie is a senior video editor at IGN based in Sydney, Australia. He has 25 years of experience covering video games, having served as Deputy Editor on Official PlayStation 2 Magazine Australia and as Editor of Official Xbox 360 Magazine Australia, before joining IGN in 2009. You can find him on Bluesky @tristanogilvie.bsky.social

item.title: Keanu Reeves is returning as John Wick in an animated film that aims to tell the assassin’s story before the tragic events of the first movie.
item.description:
Keanu Reeves is returning as John Wick in an animated film that aims to tell the assassin’s story before the tragic events of the first movie.
The animated flick will be produced by the same team that produced the John Wick movies, comprised of Thunder Road’s Basil Iwanyk and Erica Lee, 87Eleven Entertainment’s Chad Stahelski, and, of course, Keanu Reeves. Point Grey will join the group to produce, as well.
Reeves is also set to reprise his role as the ‘Baba Yaga.’ As told by Lionsgate, this movie will “go back in time to tell the story of John Wick before the first film, as he completes the Impossible Task in order to free himself from his obligation to the High Table and earn the right to be with the love of his life, Helen.” (It’ll be nice to see John Wick being happy, for once.)
Ranking the John Wick Movies
Shannon Tindle, an Emmy Award-winning director, writer, and producer known for works like Ultraman: Rising and Kubo and the Two Strings is set to direct. Screenwriting duo Ryan and Kaz Firpo are onboard to write the film; the two are known for Marvel’s Eternals.
This is the latest news we’ve gotten from this highly-anticipated project after it was first announced last year. Adam Fogelson, motion picture chair at Lionsgate, gave fans a little something to chew on during its announcement, saying, “In both animation and the world of ‘John Wick,’ the possibilities are endless. And there is no ‘John Wick’ story fans are clamoring for more than the ‘Impossible Task.’ Shannon’s take on that story is an incredible one, and we are beyond excited to see what John Wick can do in animation.”
The specific animation house responsible for bringing John Wick’s action-packed, assassin-filled world to life has not yet been officially announced. For now, it’s anyone’s guess as to what it will eventually look like, but it’s certainly exciting news while we wait for John Wick 5.
Yes, a fifth movie installment is going to happen, despite the fourth movie appearing to end on a perfect note. The film was first revealed in April 2025, with Fogelson most recently saying that director “Chad [Stahelski] and Keanu have an idea that they think can be really exciting.”
Previously, Stahelski said a script was in active development, though the actual story seemed to be eluding him and fellow writer Mike Finch.
“I’m not going to lie to you, it’s a bit of a conundrum. Me and Mike Finch — the writer on 4 who’s also writing 5 — we’ve got a pretty good story that I think is cool. Once we have a 50-page book, and if we’re feeling it, we’ll sit with Keanu and shape this thing. Look, everybody seems to want it. It’s a matter of whether we crack it. We’re actively working on it. It’s just … is it going to be satisfying?” he said in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter.
Which is your favorite John Wick movie?

item.title: Spectrum customers can get a free internet upgrade this month to download GTA 6 faster.
item.description:
Spectrum customers can get a free internet upgrade this month to download GTA 6 faster.
The company announced earlier this week that it would be a free "Gig Speed Lift" from November 9 to November 30 for existing customers. This will allow players the opportunity to download the game within 30 minutes. So, if you're planning on buying the game on day one or later in November, this will be a huge time saver. Or, if you just want to watch your pre-load complete incredibly quickly, this is also an option. You can click here to learn more about how to activate this offer if you're a Spectrum user.
Pre-loading for GTA 6 begins on November 10, and it will be an absolute beast of a game when it comes to download size. Rockstar has confirmed that the game is 212 GBs, which is nearly a quarter the size of the average PS5 (not counting the required space for the OS and other mandatory elements on the console). Given that fans are anticipating a pretty massive open-world with lots to see and do, the size makes sense. As a result, fans will want to take full advantage of the nine-day pre-load window or hop on this Spectrum deal so they can play as soon as possible.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
We're officially just two weeks away from the GTA 6's launch. Rockstar released 39 new screenshots from the game earlier today, showing off Vice City, Jason and Lucia in action, and a whole bunch of crime. The screenshots also revealed that rapper Kodak Black would be in the game as an NPC, which has fueled speculation that other musical artists would be in the game. The likes of Dr Dre, Phil Collins, and others have all been prominently featured in-game in other GTA titles, so it's not a stretch to imagine some celebrities in a modern-day Vice City.
It's unclear what else Rockstar has up its sleeve as we get closer to launch, as it released what appears to be the final trailer back in October. Some fans are expecting to hear about PS5 Pro upgrades prior to release, but beyond that, we appear to be at the end of this long marketing road.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Skarsgård opened up about Physint in a November 5 episode of Josh Horowitz’s Happy Sad Confused podcast, where he revealed that he’s a massive fan of the Metal Gear series and shared a conversation he had with Kojima regarding his love for cinema.
item.description:
In September 2026, Hollywood’s resident horror icon Bill Skarsgård was confirmed to play the lead role in Hideo Kojima’s highly anticipated action-espionage project Physint.
This game marks a long-awaited return to form from Kojima as fans pine for another Metal Gear-style experience. And while much about it is still unknown, we got just a smidge more information about the project thanks to its leading man, Bill Skarsgård.
Skarsgård opened up about the game in a November 5 episode of Josh Horowitz’s Happy Sad Confused podcast, where he revealed that he’s a massive fan of the Metal Gear series and shared a conversation he had with Kojima regarding his love for cinema.
“That’s a big deal for me,” he said. “Specifically, the Metal Gear Solid games. I played every single [one], at least the ones on [console] platform. Starting from the one on PlayStation 1 all the way to the last one. I was very enamored by [Kojima], the mythology and the universes he creates, but also the sort of mystique and allure about him, as well.
“I was really into it growing up. He is an auteur, but he’s a video game auteur. He’s fluent in filmmaking, and film, and cinema. I think at this point, I remember at one point way back, 20 years ago, there was talk of a Metal Gear solid movie. ‘Is Hideo going to direct it? Of course, I can’t wait to see him transition into film.’ I asked him, ‘Would you ever do a film?’ and he’s like, ‘No.’ At this point, what he’s doing is inventing a new medium. It is film. It’s eight hours worth of narrative, but it’s also an entire universe that you play. It truly is, quite literally, worldbuilding. Now, with technology, we’re getting closer and closer to something that's photorealistic and interactive when you play it. He’s a pioneer, and he keeps going out to untreaded waters.”
Skarsgård went on to confirm that he is providing performance capture for the game, something he already has experience with thanks to his role in Marvel’s Eternals and his extensive past working with mocap studio Goodbye Kansas (known for Alan Wake 2, God of War, Cyberpunk 2077 and many more).
This is the latest glimpse into the game we’ve gotten since the cast was revealed in September, which also includes Charlee Fraser, Don Lee, and Minami Hamabe. And in early October, Kojima discussed Physint in a podcast, saying he wants the project to “evoke the roots of Metal Gear Solid games” but be a “new interactive experience with a different kind of spy action,” as told by IGN’s Ryan McCaffrey.
Most notably, Physint recently changed hands from Sony to Xbox; in a bombshell statement, Kojima said the game faced cancellation from the PlayStation parent company, but luckily, Microsoft stepped in to keep it alive. Sources told Bloomberg the project "missed deadlines and was on track to be well over budget despite being years away from release," suggesting that PlayStation’s seemingly sudden decision to drop the game was a direct result of these issues.
For now, fans can look forward to the Death Stranding anime, as well as watch out for more from Kojima’s upcoming horror game, OD Knock, starring Hunter Schafer and Sophia Lillis. News on the Metal Gear movie continues to be sparse, with its last big update happening earlier this year when Final Destination: Bloodlines duo Zach Lipovsky and Adam B. Stein were brought on to direct.
Image Credit: Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images for BAFTA

item.title: Dr. Doom’s latest target is entertainment chain Dave and Buster’s, which has fully submitted to the Marvel villain for an expansive Avengers: Doomsday campaign.
item.description:
Dr. Doom’s latest target is entertainment chain Dave and Buster’s, which has fully submitted to the Marvel villain for an expansive Avengers: Doomsday campaign.
Starting on November 16, Dave & Buster’s is becoming Doom & Buster’s. Select locations are already rolling out ‘Doomsday Zones,’ entire sections of the arcade dedicated to the Avengers takeover. Enter the Dr. Doom archway and you’ll find a collection of Marvel games and activities in addition to new D&B drinks and prizes.
"When one of the biggest movies of the year is coming, you don't put up a poster. You bend the knee," said Jeremy Tucker, chief marketing officer at Dave & Buster's. "We gave Doom our name. We gave him the floor. We gave him the bar… All shall play."
As one of the leading arcade chains, the big tie-in is games. On Dave & Buster's floors, fans can already find a new selection of Marvel-themed activities:
Doom & Buster’s activities:
MARVEL Cosmic Invasion
Avengers: Roller Race & Battle
Thor's Hammer Strike
Avengers Themed Photo Booth
Cosmic Invasion is the big headliner here. The game dropped on PC and consoles last December, and through the D&B campaign, is now getting the full arcade cabinet treatment. Like the fully released version, the arcade edition will support up to four players.
We’re pretty big fans of the tag-team beat-em up, saying it "has the juice" in our 7/10 review, which knocks off some points for a limited hero gallery. Thankfully, the game has released plenty of new content in the past year. A new Doom-themed DLC, 'The Siege of Castle Doom,' is launching on November 10, and will presumably be included in the in-store activations.
New prizes vary across locations. The crane games are packed with their own range of Marvel-specific collectibles, including some vaguely described "new inflatables." Doomsday Zones will also feature a fully stocked Avengers Funko pusher, while kiosks offer new Avengers-themed prizes like Collectible Power Cards.
Throughout the campaign, ‘DOOMHOUR’ will strike at random times, offering customers double tickets on any green swipe games. D&B Rewards members will get a 24-hour heads up about the DOOMHOUR, while the rest of us peasants will simply have to wait for the alarm to blare. Registered members will also get access to new Rewards Challenges throughout the campaign.
Of course, Dave and Buster’s bars are also now serving a spread of Doom-themed drinks. For the alcohol-inclined, D&B offers the Doomsday's Dominion, Multiversal Mule, and Fantastic Flight. New mocktails include Panther's Potion and Captain’s Punch.
Marvel has been collaborating with everything from KFC to the MLB in the lead-up to Avengers: Doomsday, releasing in theaters on December 18. Dave & Buster’s, however, appears particularly willing to commit to the bit, which is exactly what Disney execs are looking for.
"Rather than creating a traditional promotion, they transformed their entire business into an immersive celebration of Marvel Studios' Avengers: Doomsday," said Lylle Breier, EVP of Partnerships, Promotions and Events at The Walt Disney Studios. "The result is a bold, fan-first experience that extends the story beyond the theater and into the real world in a way only Dave & Buster's could."
Was Robert Downey Jr being cast as Doctor Doom the right move for the MCU?

item.title: Curry Barker, famous for his hit horror flick Obsession, is keen on bringing his terrifying tastes to the world of Indiana Jones if the opportunity ever arises.
item.description:
Curry Barker, famous for his hit horror movie Obsession, is keen on bringing his terrifying tastes to the world of Indiana Jones if the opportunity ever arises.
Barker shared his vision for an especially grisly take on Indy’s adventures during a conversation with Gold Derby after the outlet brought up similar remarks made by Cooper Tomlinson, Barker’s longtime collaborator who co-wrote, produced, and starred in Obsession as Ian, Bear’s best friend.
"I would want to do a really f**ked up, rated-R version of [Indiana Jones],” Barker said. “I want to do a crazy adventure movie. That's something that Cooper and I have talked about, because we feel like we've never seen something like that; we've only ever seen the family-friendly version.
“But what happens if two regular guys, or one regular guy, goes on a journey that turns crazy? Literally pushing the boundaries of that genre would be fun for me."
Indiana Jones and the Great Circle Switch 2 Screenshots
As previously mentioned, Tomlinson feels a similar way, hoping to bring back the action-adventure films that defined cinema through the '80s and '90s.
"I'd love to bring back the adventure epic like Raiders of the Lost Ark," he told the outlet. "What really worked with Obsession was making something that was honest and grounded in reality; obviously we can all suspend disbelief and enjoy all the crazy action stuff that isn't real. But when it comes to the characters and story, it should be more grounded and honest. That's how we're going to get those kinds of action classics back."
Speaking of action-adventure movies that defined the '90s, Michael Johnston (who played Bear in Obsession) has been cast in the next Mummy movie, which will also feature the return of Brendan Fraser and Rachel Weisz. Also speaking with Golden Derby, he described the contrast between filming a small-budget indie horror movie like Obsession and a grand, big-budget picture like The Mummy: Book of the Dead as “really different.”
"These productions are like a well-oiled machine; we do a scene many, many times from many, many different angles, which is nice because it gives us the opportunity to work things out. That takes the pressure off in a way," he said.
"But there's also a lot more waiting around on those sets than on indie films. With something like Obsession, you only have a couple chances to get something done, and you're also helping everyone else out behind the scenes. I'm not doing that on The Mummy; I'm sitting back in my chair and enjoying the catering. But getting to work with Brendan and Rachel is great, and [directors] Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett are the most lovely guys."
The Mummy: Book of the Dead is scheduled to release on October 15, 2027. Barker’s next movie, a horror-comedy called Anything But Ghosts, is also releasing next year in May.

item.title: The Odyssey is returning to theaters in December for one last hoorah before awards season goes into full swing.
item.description:
The Odyssey is returning to theaters in December for one last hoorah before awards season goes into full swing.
Universal has announced that Christopher Nolan's R-rated epic will return to theaters on December 11 in over 1,000 cinemas across the United States and Canada. The film will be coming back to IMAX screens, including ones that support the 70MM IMAX format it was designed for. This is presumably part of a larger campaign to get The Odyssey some awards buzz ahead of the Oscars, and probably earn some extra pocket change for the studio.
The Odyssey has already made $1.8 billion at the box office to become the highest-grossing R-rated film in history. It seems hard to imagine this re-release getting it over the hump for $2 billion, as Dune Part 3 will take over premium format screens on December 18. Avengers: Doomsday will also take up as much attention for movie lovers, if not more. It's unclear if The Odyssey will continue to play on regular screens after those two movies are released, or if this is a limited one-week run.
The Odyssey Images
The Odyssey is a favorite for many of the big prestigious awards, with many expecting a Best Picture nomination, Best Actor for Matt Damon, Best Director for Christopher Nolan, and many more. Whether it scores all of the nominations it's expected to get remains to be seen. It'll also be interesting to see what awards it could win, as Nolan's last film, Oppenheimer, cleaned house at the Oscars in 2023. It's rare for a filmmaker to win big twice in a row, though not unheard of. Alejandro González Iñárritu won Best Director back-to-back years in 2014 and 2015 for Birdman and The Revenant, respectively.
Nevertheless, it'll be a busy time at the movie theater in December with the return of The Odyssey and some of the year's heaviest hitters with Dune and Avengers. For those who aren't interested in venturing out into the cold to see Nolan's latest film again, The Odyssey is also coming to home video later this month.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: G2 Esports has parted ways with its head coach, Luka "Perkz" Perković, following divisive comments he made in a lengthy post on Twitter/X.
item.description:
G2 Esports has parted ways with its head coach and retired League of Legends player Luka "Perkz" Perković following divisive comments he made in a lengthy post on Twitter/X.
The 2,676-word-long tweet was published on November 4, 2026. Perković described it as his “first and last honest post in [the] last decade,” where he could “address some things honestly.” He explained that he’d written the statement to clarify his stance on certain topics “so that, at the very least, you can hate me for what I really stand for, and then that's completely fine by me.”
In the post, which he jokingly called a “tweet bomb,” Perković said he is not a fan of and does not endorse the Tate brothers in any way; claimed that “doesn’t really do politics” and has never “ever voted once” in his life; said he is not a fan of either Donald Trump or Kamala Harris; said he is a devout Catholic; denied being a “Putin fanboy” or being on the side of Russia in the war on Ukraine; and shared his stance on abortion, comparing it to “murder.”
League of Legends Classic Screenshots
“I don’t really do politics, nor have I even ever voted once in my life. I do have opinions, and I wish I was more educated on the topic, but the truth is I’m not, so I stay away from it,” he wrote. “There are some things I stand for, very simple things in life, but the only thing that is unshakeable for me, how it’s so widely accepted in public, is abortion. I cannot comprehend how people do not understand that is a muder, as life is created at conception. That is one view I will die by and never change.”
Perković also addressed his relationship with retired League of Legends pro and former G2 CEO Carlos "ocelote" Rodríguez Santiago, who stepped down from the company in 2022 after sharing a video of himself at a party with Andrew Tate. “Me standing up for Carlos publicly when he was being cancelled has nothing to [do] with all the things I’m all accused of supporting. Trafficking? Misogyny? Nazism? War? Are you okay?” Perković said of the matter.
“Carlos believed in me when nobody else did. I did not have a close relationship with my family when I was 16, including my parents, [who] I was not too close with, either. …Carlos and I have gone both completely different ways. He is his own person and I’m completely my own. In the end Carlos’ ego is something that put an end to his esports career, which was f**king insane. So there is a lesson to be learned in there, as well. We have a lot of different views on life.”
Perhaps the biggest takeaway from Perković’s post was his stance on abortion. This particular remark was a main talking point among fans and fellow players on social media, sparking a massive wave of backlash against him. G2 Esports addressed the situation in a public post mere hours later, where they confirmed that they have parted ways with Perković due to his tweet.
Their full statement is as follows:
“Last night, like many of you, we saw the statement shared by the Head Coach of one of our teams. G2 is a diverse and international organization with different people from all around the world. While the world is complex and not everyone agrees on everything, some of the statements made last night do not align with G2's stance and values. We have fans with different cultures and personal opinions, and it is of the utmost importance to us as an organisation that we respect and uphold this diversity when representing G2. We acknowledge that this statement hurt many of our fans, and we want to apologize for it.
“As a result, we have decided to terminate our collaboration with the individual. We will now focus on rebuilding our staff and roster for the next season and ask for your patience, as we will not be able to communicate any changes until free agency officially opens. - Alban Dechelotte, CEO of G2.”
Perković has since published one other tweet — a Bible verse from Luke 6:22. “Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake,” he wrote. This post, too, has received backlash from users. Perković has not posted anything else on his account at the time of writing.

item.title: The ending of Godzilla Minus Zero leaves just enough room for a continuation of the story filmmaker Takashi Yamazaki has crafted, but the writer/director says he's split on whether or not he'd want to come back to it.
item.description:
Godzilla Minus Zero writer/director Takashi Yamazaki told The Hollywood Reporter that he's "fifty-fifty" on whether or not he'd come back to make a third Godzilla film.
Extremely minor Godzilla Minus Zero spoilers ahead!
"I’m quite satisfied and happy with the current ending we have," Yakazaki said when asked about the film's ambiguous ending that leaves just enough room for a continuation of the story. "It entrusts the interpretation to the audience in terms of how they want to receive it and what they want to walk out of theaters with. That being said, if Godzilla Minus Zero is my last Godzilla film, that would make me a bit sad. I do have other films lined up, starting with Grandgear and a few others, but at some point in my career, I would love to revisit Godzilla and see how we can expand this world."
Grandgear was announced in 2024 as Yamazaki's first major Hollywood studio movie, with Sony Pictures, and his first English-language feature film. It's currently slated for a February 18, 2028 release. Starring Sam Nivola (The White Lotus Season 3), Nico Parker (The Last of Us, the live-action How to Train Your Dragon), and Paul Giamatti (it's Paul Giamatti...), Grandgear is a live-action sci-fi mecha movie, something Yamazaki also told THR was "something I’ve always wanted to do." Yamazaki is writing and directing, and Bad Robot is producing.
But first, Godzilla Minus Zero comes out in U.S. theaters this weekend, a mere three years after Godzilla Minus One became a box-office sensation in 2023 on a reportedly tiny $10–15 million budget and a lean 35-person VFX team, with Yamazaki overseeing. It went on to win the Oscar for Best Visual Effects, marking the first time a Japanese film took home the award, and did it with the tiniest budget of any category winner in more than a decade.
Yamazaki told IGN that, when writing Godzilla Minus Zero, he had to set aside the need to try and one-up everything he had accomplished with Godzilla Minus One. “I think it's very dangerous to create a movie with that type of mindset because you're going to risk diluting what makes the movie great in the first place," he said. "So those are the wrong reasons to make a movie and it ends up becoming an antagonist in your moviemaking process.”
Godzilla Minus Zero is both the first R-rated Godzilla movie and the first Japanese film to be specifically shot for IMAX screens. It's also very loud! We said it was Good in our review, calling out its "satisfying and visually amazing scenes of giant-monster destruction."
But back to the potential of a third Godzilla movie. Turning these films into a trilogy raises a critical question: What would it be called, after the naming convention has already counted down from Minus One to Minus Zero? I have a pitch: Godzilla Plus One that, of course, introduces another new kaiju. Toho, call me!
Leanne Butkovic (she/they) is an Editorial Programming Manager at IGN, where they've also written about TV, movies, and games.

item.title: Hot on the heels of Bethesda Game Studios officially announcing the full name of its highly anticipated next project, The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, the developer has already put up merch for the upcoming RPG on its online shop. You can be the first person in your friend group with a Sentinel-logo hoodie or t-shirt. And like the Ford Model T, it comes in any color you want, as long as it's black.
item.description:
Hot on the heels of Bethesda Game Studios officially announcing the full name of its highly anticipated next project, The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, the developer has already put up merch for the upcoming RPG on its online shop. You can be the first person in your friend group with a Sentinel-logo hoodie or T-shirt. And like the Ford Model T, it comes in any color you want, as long as it's black.
The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel hoodie is $64.99, while the identical item in T-shirt form is $34.99. Hat tip to @MrMattyPlays on X for first spotting the Sentinel merch. Bethesda says, "Celebrate The Elder Scrolls VI. Your next journey through Tamriel will be in The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Show off your excitement with the official hoodie!" And if you're interesteed in ordering, note the disclaimer: "This hoodie runs small. For the perfect fit, we recommend ordering one size larger than your usual size." The T-shirt shares an identical description, minus the note about it running small.
You'll have plenty of time to break in either of these clothing items, as Sentinel isn't expected to be released for at least a couple more years. That would mean it might be at least a decade between the original announcement of The Elder Scrolls 6 and the time it's finally on your hard drive. Regardless, it's arguably the biggest game Xbox has in its portfolio by a country mile and when the release date finally arrives, it's going to be a very, very big deal.
Amidst all of the changes at Xbox this year, it will be interesting to see if, a) The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel will be available on Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on day one, b) if it might line up with the launch of Xbox's next-gen Project Helix console/gaming PC hybrid, and/or c) if it ends up being an Xbox console exclusive.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: The last two years of BioWare's life were filmed and will be shown in a new documentary about the game studio.
item.description:
The last two years of BioWare's life were filmed and will be shown in a new documentary about the game studio.
The documentary, titled Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, will show the studio's journey over the last few years. While it's unclear if this will include new footage of the canceled Mass Effect game, it is a rare peek behind the curtain and likely a raw one, given how the story ends. Industry veteran Geoff Keighley revealed that he was interviewed for the film earlier this year, and confirmed that it will be released sometime in 2027.
The project is being produced by Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie for Canada‘s Super Channel, as BioWare was primarily a Canadian studio. It's unclear if it will also be made available online for those outside of Canada. The documentary will feature exclusive interviews and insights from BioWare talent, such as Mass Effect game director Casey Hudson, Jennifer Hale (voice actress for the female variant of Commander Shepard), and many more. It should be an interesting watch whenever it is released.
“When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honoured and genuinely moved,” said BioWare co-founders Dr. Ray Muzyka and Dr. Greg Zeschuk. “BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about deeply emotionally engaging stories and characters, brought to life by the amazingly talented people on our dev teams, and our excellent production and distribution partners who helped us bring those stories successfully to all corners of the planet, and our passionate fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honours those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again.”
11 Mass Effect Characters and Moments the TV Show Needs to Be a Hit
BioWare was shut down last month, much to the shock of the wider industry and fans alike. The studio had been struggling for a while; its last three games were misfires, and the next Mass Effect game was expected to still be years away. As a result, EA reportedly decided to place its bets on a new Star Wars Battlefront game from DICE and Respawn instead of continuing to fund a new Mass Effect game.
A trailer for Mass Effect 5, which was apparently called Mass Effect Universe, did find its way online, painting a better picture of what fans could've expected from the canceled game. Some fans have held out hope that the Mass Effect IP could be acquired by another company, but as of right now, it doesn't seem like that's in the cards.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: A 52-year-old Japanese YouTuber is learning karate by studying characters’ moves from Tekken after his son inspired him to pursue a journey in martial arts.
item.description:
A 52-year-old Japanese YouTuber is learning karate by studying characters’ moves from Tekken 3 after his son inspired him to pursue a journey in martial arts.
AskJapan is a fairly popular YouTuber with more than 189,000 subscribers. He’s best known for his vlog-style videos where he chats with viewers and plays retro video games on old-school consoles, often while dressing up in low-budget cosplay of characters from the games he’s playing.
He’s been on a fighting game stint lately, taking on the likes of Street Fighter II and Tekken 3, the latter of which he’s using to help himself learn real-life martial arts moves. He explained this newfound interest in a November 3 video, saying one of his son’s recent karate demonstrations made him inspired to try it out for himself.
Tekken 8 - Exclusive Screens
AskJapan says that his son is a brown belt, a rank that’s right beneath the black belt (the top level that signifies total mastery of the art). He’s only 10 years old, and has been training since he was 5. This fact, combined with his son’s latest “overwhelming” karate demonstration, made him want to try it out for himself. But rather than hitting the dojo first, AskJapan is taking an unconventional approach to the art; he’s taking ‘lessons’ from Tekken characters.
“His performance inspired my spirit, my motivation,” the YouTuber explained. “I thought, ‘Okay, maybe someday in the future, I [can] start karate, even though I’m 52. Why not? I realized that, to start, I have to practice karate with games. That’s why I was determined today, after watching my son’s performance this morning. Why not start today, and practice with Tekken? This is my way of improving.”
Throughout the rest of the video, he took notes from Tekken 3 as he played through the game on a homemade ‘arcade cabinet’ that he’d fashioned out of cardboard. It’s an extremely charming watch — but his second foray into the game was downright hilarious.
His next video, which he uploaded on November 4, shows him fashioning a Heihachi cosplay out of a helmet and cardboard paper. His goal was to unlock the boss character by attempting to beat Tekken 3’s arcade mode, but he unfortunately failed.
Fans are rallying behind the YouTuber on his latest mission, sharing words of encouragement for both his martial arts goals and his journey to becoming a better Tekken player.
“There is no age to start karate, and you still look in shape,” one viewer wrote.
“I hope Harada and the gang see this and appreciate it like I do,” another said, referencing the former Tekken boss.
It’s true that having martial arts experience can come in handy; earlier this year, a member of the fighting game community went viral for using skills he’d learned from sumo wrestling to fend off a knife-wielding man at his local gaming cafe. And despite the shocking ordeal, he returned to his Twitch stream straight afterward, complaining that the incident had cost him 14 LP in League of Legends.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Electronic Arts is bringing 25 classic games from its library to Steam today, including seven Anniversary Editions for six Wing Commander games as well as Road Rash. The rest of the re-releases include every Ultima RPG, both Crusader games, Strike Commander, and Theme Hospital. The 18 re-releases are $4.99 each, while the quality-of-life-updated Anniversary Editions cost $9.99 each.
item.description:
Electronic Arts is bringing 25 classic games from its library to Steam today, including seven Anniversary Editions for six Wing Commander games as well as Road Rash. The rest of the re-releases include every Ultima RPG, both Crusader games, Strike Commander, and Theme Hospital. The 18 re-releases are $4.99 each, while the quality-of-life-updated Anniversary Editions cost $9.99 each.
Regarding those quality-of-life updates, EA says that means that these refreshed versions "support modern systems, controls, improve performance and make the titles more approachable without compromising their authenticity." Regarding Wing Commander specifically, which is perhaps best remembered for its many full-motion video (FMV) cutscenes starring Mark Hamill, the companys says, "For each restored Wing Commander title, these improvements were made possible by the dedicated community, who were open and eager to collaborate with the passionate team at EA to incorporate their mods into the official releases. This launch is a celebration of the community’s commitment to the franchise, which is why anyone who already owns a digital copy of the Wing Commander titles on GOG or the EA App will automatically receive the Anniversary Edition upgrade for free on their respective digital platform."
For each of the Anniversary Editions, including my personal favorite, Road Rash (check out the trailer above), EA says, "The Anniversary Editions have been a labor of love, inspired by the discovery of a physical media vault containing thousands of Betacam, VHS, and D1 tapes alongside other media assets. The digitization process recovered the supposedly lost Master FMV sequences for these seven legendary titles, which were meticulously re-edited to restore the over 1,500 cinematic scenes across these games."
The Ultima series, meanwhile, was the brainchild of legendary RPG designer Richard "Lord British" Garriott, who went on to build a castle for a house and later become one of the first private citizens to go into outer space. You can hear about those stories and more on my old IGN Unfiltered interview with him from 2017.
Here's the full list of classic games EA is re-releasing:

item.title: GOG is old enough to drink in the UK. To celebrate that milestone, the DRM-free storefront — which lets players do what they want to games once they own them, including sending them to other PCs, backing them up to hard drives, and even burning them onto discs to add to a physical collection — has announced a range of surprises.
item.description:
GOG is old enough to drink in the UK. To celebrate that milestone, the DRM-free storefront — which lets players do what they want to games once they own them, including sending them to other PCs, backing them up to hard drives, and even burning them onto discs to add to a physical collection — has announced a range of surprises.
The company is currently on a mission to keep games available to play even after the seasons end and servers close down. Its GOG Patrons initiative has saved 300 old games, funding them to be made compatible with modern operating systems. Over 10,000 patrons have signed up to help. The latest game to benefit from this was Nox, the action RPG developed and published by Westwood Studios and EA back in 2000.
“We dig deep into the code, fixing long-lasting bugs, adjusting screen resolutions, adding controller support, missing cutscenes and much, much more,” said Marcin Paczynski, senior business development manager.
GOG has made over 1,700 fixes to old games in its preservation program. Next up, there’s good news for classic space sim and Mark Hamill fans.
The Wing Commander series — Wing Commander 1-4 games, Prophecy Gold, and Privateer 2 — is getting an anniversary edition update. GOG collaborated with modders for Prophecy, with a goal of making the game more approachable, adding controller support to offer a new way to play.
Each of these games comes with the legacy version and the touched up Anniversary Edition. For people who already own the original games on GOG, the Anniversary Editions are free to download at launch.
Ahead of those updated space sims, there’s something new on GOG right now: Road Rash. The violent motorbike racing classic got the same treatment as Wing Commander, making it compatible with modern systems and control inputs.
GOG also announced Retro Vibe, a publishing arm focused on “new games with a classic soul.” Retro Vibe releases include a VHS-fuzzed FPS with Max Payne-esque bullet time called Cop Bastard, a side-scrolling shooter with tough boss battles called The Looter, tactical cyberpunk RPG Shardpunk 2, boomer shooter with massive boomsticks Project Warlock: Lost Chapters, and the mysterious greyscale indie game After Hell Freezes Over.
You can Wishlist the full lineup of games and check them out in more detail on GOG.com. It’s a site GOG is hoping you’ll spend more time on anyway, as the service is also introducing GOG Social, a new gaming forum integrated with your game library, allowing you to tag games in posts, taking readers directly to the store page. The forum has marked spoilers, threaded replies, reactions, post edits, media support, bookmarks, topic subscriptions, and more.
Lastly, GOG Galaxy — GOG’s launcher that lets you combine your entire library from different stores into one space — is also coming to Linux. It’s landing with new customization and personalization options. Watch the entire showcase on the GOG YouTube channel.
